Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks good for our inference workloads. Procurement asked me to follow up on a couple of marketplace-specific questions before we escalate to legal:

1) EdgeScale's preference is to keep the published list price steady in the AWS Marketplace but move commercial economics into an earnback-style credit that posts month-over-month — this helps with internal price comparisons. Can Redwood support: a 12-month commit with a monthly usage-based earnback credit (2% of invoiced usage) rather than a one-time up-front discount?

2) We work with a reseller (CloudResell) who will invoice us separately for integration services and expects a 6% commission on gross list price. How do you typically route reseller commission for private offers? Do you: a) reduce the list price we see in the marketplace, b) issue a separate pass-through payment to the reseller, or c) credit the reseller through the marketplace seller fee? We need to understand invoicing pathing for our finance team.

3) Any documentation or exemplar MA/PO language you can share would help speed procurement/legal review.

We want to lock economics this week if possible — can you send a sample structure and an updated quote?

Hi Emily — great to meet you (and thanks for the clear follow-up). Short answer: yes, we can support an earnback credit model while keeping list prices stable; we just need to align routing and gross-to-net treatment. Details below and next steps at the bottom.

Proposed structure (recommended for speed):
- Term: 12 months committed consumption (monthly billing through AWS Marketplace)
- List price: Keep published SKU list price unchanged in Marketplace (no downlist)
- Earnback credit: Redwood to apply a monthly post-invoice credit to EdgeScale equal to 2% of billed usage during the previous month. Credit will appear as a separate line item on the following month’s Redwood invoice (gross-to-net will be visible in our finance export).
- Reseller commission (CloudResell): Two options we can support — preference and operational implications below.

Option A — Pass-through reseller invoice (recommended for EdgeScale finance):
  - Redwood issues customer invoices at full list price via Marketplace (no reduction).
  - Reseller (CloudResell) invoices EdgeScale separately for services; EdgeScale pays reseller directly.
  - Redwood does not mediate the reseller commission. This keeps Marketplace reporting simple but requires EdgeScale to handle separate payments/POs for the reseller.

Option B — Reseller paid via marketplace seller fee (cleaner for one-pay):
  - Redwood retains a portion of the Marketplace payout to pay CloudResell (we route via seller_fee).
  - Net to EdgeScale remains list price; CloudResell receives commission from Redwood settlement.
  - Requires reseller onboarding as a payout recipient (we can expedite but need KYC).

Operational notes and implications:
- Gross-to-net: If you want credits to look like off-invoice adjustments (not reducing list price), we will surface earnback credits as separate credit memos rather than changing SKU list price. That preserves comparability in Marketplace catalogs.
- Tax & accounting: Laura — tagging for tax implications and invoice pathing; should we flag a specific accounting code for earnback credits (e.g., 6503-EAR) or let finance map post-hoc?
- Legal: We will provide a short MA template that captures the earnback schedule and invoice-credit mechanics. See attached draft MA and a sample pricing workbook (attached).

Next steps:
1) Emily — confirm which reseller option you prefer (Pass-through vs seller_fee).
2) If seller_fee, we need reseller contact and KYC paperwork (we can send intake form).
3) If pass-through, let us know if you want Redwood to provide an internal helper note for your procurement team to show invoice examples.
4) I'll attach an updated one-pager quote (spreadsheet) with commit tiers and sample monthly credit schedule — you should have that in your inbox in 30–60 minutes.

Thanks — looping in Ben on channel economics and Laura on billing.

Best,

Thanks Maya — quick note from channel/ops side.

If EdgeScale wants CloudResell to receive 6% of gross list price, we recommend Option B (seller_fee) only if: a) CloudResell signs our reseller payout form and KYC, b) legal approves the payout routing, and c) EdgeScale is comfortable with Redwood showing a net payout breakdown in the Marketplace settlement (we can redact sensitive components if needed).

If you prefer pass-through (Option A), please confirm whether CloudResell will issue invoices to EdgeScale with a separate PO number. We find many enterprise finance teams prefer pass-through because it keeps their vendor ledger intact.

One practical clarification: our standard seller_fee flow reduces the cash payout Redwood receives from Marketplace before we remit to the reseller — that means from a revenue recognition standpoint we record the full list price and then record the reseller commission as a contra-revenue (or cost of sale). If EdgeScale needs the reseller commission to be treated as a procurement expense (not a reduction in Redwood revenue), pass-through is cleaner.

Laura — pinging you for confirmation on accounting code and whether we need a different invoice template.
